articles.title: 1 vs. 100 Live Was the Kind of Incredible Creative Risk I'd Like to See Xbox Get Back To
articles.summary: I so vividly remember making the time to log on and play 1 vs. 100 in the evenings the game was available, and trying to answer those trivia questions as quickly as possible. You could get on Party Chat with your friends and root for each other to make it into The Mob -- or even The One.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

To this day, the Achievements on my Xbox gamercard that I'm most proud of are the 12 out of 12 I got in 1 vs. 100. They are, of course, impossible to attain now, and so I will always cherish them. But 1 vs. 100 was more than a licensed video game adaptation of a popular game show. For Xbox, it was an incredibly gutsy creative risk that actually worked, and I'd love to see the company get back to that kind of boldness again.

articles.title: I'm Getting My Hopes Up for The Ascent 2 After the Developer Told Me It Had Big Franchise Plans
articles.summary: The Ascent 2 is a game I’ve hoped developer Neon Giant would make ever since I finished the wonderful The Ascent back in 2021 — and after speaking to the studio at gamescom, I’m convinced it’s now in the works.
body: Neon Giant is currently hard at work on No Law, a first-person Cyberpunk-style game with immersive sim elements set to be published by parent company Krafton. But it has also confirmed plans to turn The Ascent, which has had over 12 million players, into a franchise.

“It's something we always wanted to do,” creative director and co-founder Arcade Berg told me. “Creatively, after we were done with the first The Ascent — that was a smashing success for us — creatively, we just wanted to go somewhere else. We weren't ready to do more The Ascent there and then. And team size and also investment wise, we weren't prepared for multiple projects.

“But one of the great things that we are now working with Krafton is that we now have backing and support that we can take creative risks. So together with them, we've actually built a franchise plan. We're moving The Ascent from a game to a franchise. And we'll be dropping more news as we figure things out, because it's a longer-term plan. But it's really exciting for us to now know that we have backing and support to do more. And what that is, I can't really go into details of.”

articles.title: Two Nintendo Directs Announced For Next Week, Including A Zelda Presentation
articles.summary: Not one, but two Nintendo Directs are coming next week. Nintendo has confirmed that a Legend of Zelda Direct will be held on September 8 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET, and it'll be followed by a Nintendo Direct on September 9 at the same times.
body: Rumors of a Nintendo Direct began picking up earlier this week after Ubisoft announced that a new look at Just Dance: Decades of Hits was on the way. It's worth noting that the publisher announced it for September 10, but given how often Just Dance games appear in Nintendo broadcasts, it was assumed this would be the date of a Nintendo Direct. With Nintendo hosting a September Nintendo Direct almost every year for the past decade--with 2024 being an exception--it looked like it was only a matter of time before the broadcast was officially announced.

As for what you can expect, Nintendo is keeping its lips zipped for now. Last year's September Direct was focused on several first-party games, smaller third-party titles, and the surprise reveal of a new Virtual Boy headset designed for Switch consoles, so we're guessing that it'll be more of the same for 2026. Following the release of the Switch 2 in 2025 and a steady stream of first-party games, 2026 has been slower by comparison, so here's hoping we get to see what new experiences Nintendo is working on. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is out later this month, so we'll probably get a new trailer for the turn-based tactics game.

articles.title: Odyssey Translator Emily Wilson, Who Slammed Nolan's Movie, Retranslating Homer’s Epic From Scratch
articles.summary: Emily Wilson strikes again! The University of Pennsylvania professor’s 2017 translation of The Odyssey was an inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster movie adaptation, a film that Wilson has slammed as “abysmal” in two recent op-eds that went viral.
body: “It’s a complete retranslation. It’s not a revision of the old version,” Wilson told The Associated Press. “I’m about halfway through.”
As the AP and the academics they spoke with point out, it’s exceedingly rare for a translator to issue another translation of the same work from scratch.

In her first op-ed criticizing Nolan’s The Odyssey, Wilson said she would “be ashamed to have written any part of this script” and that Nolan’s film “lacks psychological, emotional, political, and ethical depth."

Wilson called Nolan’s Odyssey “itself a kind of Trojan horse. The script grandly insists on the importance of human kindness, while the camera shows us an entirely different set of values. In these times of hatred and misinformation, we need more than the ‘apparent magic’ of deceptive images. We need art that is truthful about the costs and the necessity of compassion, and that recognizes that a sense of spiritual superiority may not protect us from lies.”

articles.title: Steam Has Generated $15 Billion In Revenue So Far In 2026, And New Games Are A Big Part Of It
articles.summary: As the platform that gets the lion's share of PC game sales, Steam naturally makes a lot of money every year from commissions, publishing fees, and more through its storefront. But how much cash has it made so far in 2026?
body: Steam's top releases by gross revenue include AAA games and breakout indie hits, with Forza Horizon 6 leading the charge. The new racing game earned Steam $210.5 million in revenue, while Crimson Desert sales were responsible for $203.3 million, Resident Evil Requiem made just over $200.9 million, and Slay the Spire 2 brought in over $148 million. Rounding out the list is Subnautica 2 at $139.2 million and Meccha Chameleon at $89.8 million.

Looking ahead, Steam's coffers can expect an influx of cash from highly anticipated releases like Phantom Blade Zero, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Gears of War: E-Day, just to name a few. Valve gets a cut from whatever is sold on Steam, including the lucrative microtransactions and DLC that accompany most games these days. Elliot also spoke to GameSpot recently about what goes into a game price tag as part of our Cheap Week deep-dives.

articles.title: GTA 6 Online Could Struggle To Pull Players Away From GTA Online, Says Valve Veteran
articles.summary: What's the biggest question about Grand Theft Auto 6? Easily Rockstar's plans for GTA Online, and how it'll factor into the post-launch plans of GTA 6. Considering just how consistently popular GTA Online has been for the developer, it is strange that Rockstar has yet to publicly comment on the…
body: As Valve veteran Chet Faliszek pointed out, Rockstar might be caught between a rock and a hard place. GTA Online continues to be a big money-maker for Rockstar and its parent group, Take-Two Interactive, but moving people to a GTA 6 online mode is a challenging prospect. As Faliszek explained, a lot of GTA Online players are heavily invested in the game, and thanks to GTA 5 regularly going on sale--or being given away for free through various programs--access to it has been cheap and easy.

"What are they going to do? That's a mess. We can all look through recent history--without pointing fingers--and see some people who did it by total replacement. We can see people who tried to win people over, and when that didn't happen, shut down the other thing," Faliszek said.

Rockstar and Take-Two would likely want to move people over to the new GTA Online as soon as possible, but forcing people to make a fresh start could be an uphill battle. As people have pointed out, major updates for GTA Online could slow as Rockstar instead focuses on GTA 6, which would be a slow death for the groundbreaking mode.
points: What's the biggest question about Grand Theft Auto 6?
Easily Rockstar's plans for GTA Online, and how it'll factor into the post-launch plans of GTA 6.

articles.title: Alien: Earth Is Officially Back as Season 2 Filming Kicks Off
articles.summary: One of the best shows of 2025 was Alien: Earth, Noah Hawley's sci-fi horror series set in the legendary universe launched by Ridley Scott's 1979 masterpiece. Following positive reactions from critics and audiences, Disney renewed the show for a second season on Nov. 11, 2025.
body: FX posted a short video to its official Instagram account on Sept. 3, announcing that production on season 2 has begun. The video is only about ten seconds and shows some of the behind-the-scenes action on set. Production on season 1 took roughly five months, with a mid-production break due to the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike. If season 2 follows a similar schedule, it should finish production in early 2027.

Creator Noah Hawley is returning as showrunner alongside most of the cast, led by Sydney Chandler as Wendy. Season 2 will also add Peter Dinklage, Tracey Ullman, Sam Spruell, and Jerome Flynn. Hawley previously worked with Spruell on Fargo, while Dinklage and Flynn starred alongside each other in Game of Thrones.

It is a good time to be an Alien fan right now. In addition to Alien: Earth Season 2, there are at least two other major projects in the works. The 2014 game Alien: Isolation is finally getting a sequel, and it looks even scarier than the original. The game will take place on an Earth-like colony and will follow a new protagonist who is not Amanda Ripley, according to Sega.

body: Similarly to the Greek-mythology-based Percy Jackson novels, The Kane Chronicles focuses on Egyptian mythology. The series centers on siblings Carter and Sadie Kane, magicians who are descended from the two pharaohs, Narmer and Ramses the Great, as they interact with Egyptian gods and goddesses. The series consists of three books released between 2010 and 2012: The Red Pyramid, The Throne of Fire, and The Serpent’s Shadow. The novels are set in the same universe as Percy Jackson.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson’s New Book Officially Solves His Biggest Sci-Fi Mystery, 8 Years Later
articles.summary: Over the course of four books and three novellas co-written by Sanderson and Janci Patterson, humanity is able to defeat the Superiority and earn their freedom to explore the stars once more.
body: Brandon Sanderson’s YA sci-fi series Skyward takes place in a far future where most of humanity is confined to isolated preserves run by aliens. After unlocking psionic powers dubbed cytonics, humanity begins to explore the stars and conquer the worlds of more peaceful species. At some point during the series of conflicts dubbed the Human Wars, Earth vanished, and humanity was conquered by an alien alliance called the Superiority. Sanderson established much of the series’ foundational lore for the Cytoverse in the 2008 short story “Defending Elysium,” and the Human Wars and life on Earth are effectively ancient history as of the beginning of Skyward, which was released in 2018.
“The question about Earth was my favorite of the hooks that were left from the previous series,” Patterson tells Polygon. “It had to be pretty hidden or they would have found it.”

articles.summary: The Starcraft website is suffering from some mysterious visual glitches and distortion roughly a week before BlizzCon. As a result, fans of the RTS series are fiercely speculating on a possible reveal.
body: The website, which currently promotes Starcraft Remastered, is showing jittering text and background art the moment you click on it. Scrolling down, the same effect is causing distortion for embedded videos of Starcraft Remastered gameplay. Something is clearly going on, but given there's no flashing 'Starcraft 3' or anything obvious like that, what this is actually hinting at remains unclear.

Taking a gander at the Starcraft Subreddit, a mix of reignited hopes and dejected pessimism. "Anything but a mobile game and we’ll all be stoked," wrote user HerdofBuffalo. Another user Iceblue responded with "It’ll be a mahjong game", while others posted "do you guys not have phones" in reference to an infamous moment during the Diablo Immortal reveal a few years ago.

This website tease is noteworthy for two reasons. As mentioned earlier, BlizzCon is scheduled to take place starting the 10th September, and given there's no dedicated Starcraft panel nor event, anything that'll be shown off will likely be taking a spot during the opening ceremony.

articles.title: No Law was one of the most exciting games I saw at Gamescom: a cyberpunk immersive sim that solves one of Deus Ex's biggest problems
articles.summary: Sometimes you see a game and can tell that the developers just get it. No Law is one of those games. Having seen it first hand at Gamescom, it has quickly become one of my most anticipated games from the show.
body: But first, what is No Law? It's a first person FPS set in a cyberpunk setting. That topline description does the game a disservice: it is an intelligently built immersive sim from Swedish developer Neon Giant that not only freshens up a setting that's starting to feel a bit played out, but also offers solutions to long-lasting genre gripes.

It achieves all this while placing you in the shoes of a bulky, hirsute giant of a man. Grey Harkner, a retired military man content to water his plants in peace, is pulled back into a world of violence and intrigue. Why this happened, and who the big players are behind the events of No Law, are mysteries to be uncovered by this walking, talking ode to action movie protagonists of the 90s and earlier. More Jean Claude Van Damme than, well, Keanu Reeves.
